title: Run of the bit appender before its final step
statement: Let $b$ be a Boolean bit and $x$ a Boolean input word. For every $j\le |x|$, the bit-appending machine on input $x$, after $j$ steps from its initial configuration, is in its scan configuration with state present, input-head position $j+1$, and output equal to the first $j$ bits of $x$.
replaced:
For every $j \le \abs{x}$, after $j$ steps from its initial configuration
on input $x$ the bit appender is at input position $j$ with output exactly
the first $j$ bits of $x$; the appending halt is still ahead.
